title: Finite-window coefficient lift of a relatively pseudo-coherent affine complex
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $B\to A$ a homomorphism of commutative rings, and $R$ a commutative finite type $B$-algebra (a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables). Put $R_A=R\otimes_B A$, and fix a surjection $P=A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\twoheadrightarrow R_A$ with $r\geq0$. Let $K\in D(R_A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be such that its restriction to $D(P)$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every $a\in\mathbf Z$, there exist a commutative finite type $B$-algebra $D$, a factorization $B\to D\to A$, and $L\in D(R_D)$, where $R_D=R\otimes_B D$, whose cohomology modules are finitely generated over $R_D$ and zero outside a finite interval, together with a morphism $\gamma:L\to\operatorname{Res}_{R_D}^{R_A}K$. The following morphism in $D(R_D)$ has cone with zero cohomology in every degree $i\geq a$:
$$A\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}L\xrightarrow{1\otimes\gamma}A\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\mu_K}K.$$
Here restriction of scalars is termwise, $R_D\to R_A$ is the given map, derived tensor is computed using a K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], and $\mu_K$ is induced by the ordinary $A$-action on an $R_A$-module complex representing $K$. Cones have the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. No flatness of any ring map is assumed, and no exact descent of $K$ is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial surjection $Q_B=B[x_1,\ldots,x_s]\twoheadrightarrow R$ from the hypothesis that $R$ is finite type. For a coefficient stage $D$ put $Q_D=D[x_1,\ldots,x_s]$; tensoring the displayed quotient gives a surjection $Q_D\twoheadrightarrow R_D$. In particular $Q_A\twoheadrightarrow R_A$. The polynomial-presentation invariance lemma, applied to this surjection and the given $P\twoheadrightarrow R_A$, makes $K$ pseudo-coherent over $Q_A$. Its bounded-above finite-free representative supplies an integer $b$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$.

proof.text: For $n=b+1$ take $D=B$, $L=0$ in $D(R)$ and $\gamma=0$. Its normalized scalar-action map is $0\to K$ and its cone is $K$, hence has zero cohomology in degrees $i\geq n$. We induct downwards on $n$, maintaining: $D$ is finite type over $B$, $B\to D\to A$ is a factorization, $L\in D(R_D)$ has bounded finitely generated cohomology, and the cone of $\theta_D=\mu_K(1\otimes\gamma):A\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}L\to K$ has $H^i=0$ for $i\geq n$. No transition map between successive models is part of the invariant.

proof.text: Consider a stage of the invariant. The rings $D$ and $Q_D$ are Noetherian by finite-type permanence. Restrict $L$ along the surjection $Q_D\twoheadrightarrow R_D$. Each cohomology module is still finitely generated over $Q_D$ (the same generators work) and is zero outside the same interval. The Noetherian pseudo-coherence criterion therefore gives a bounded-above finite-free $Q_D$-complex $E$ representing this restriction. Each term is free over $D$, since the monomials are a $D$-basis of $Q_D$. The bounded-above flat-complex lemma makes $E$ K-flat over $D$ as well as over $Q_D$. Thus $A\otimes_D E=Q_A\otimes_{Q_D}E$ represents the source of the $Q_A$-linear extension--restriction counit composite $\theta_Q$ associated to $\gamma$. It is bounded-above finite free over $Q_A$, so is pseudo-coherent. After forgetting to $Q_D$, this map has the same underlying derived scalar-action map as $\theta_D$: restriction of $\gamma$ is used, and both counits send an ordinary scalar tensor $a\otimes k$ to $ak$. Equivalently, resolve $A$ over $D$ for both counits; the comparison to the ordinary tensor is the augmentation followed by this multiplication. Hence their cones have the same underlying cohomology groups. No $R_A$-module structure on the derived tensor source is asserted.

proof.text: Let $C_Q=\operatorname{Cone}(\theta_Q)$ in $D(Q_A)$. Both its source and target are pseudo-coherent. Apply the equivalence with $m$-pseudo-coherence for every $m$ and the ring cone lemma (source parameter $m+1$, target parameter $m$); it follows that $C_Q$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$. The invariant and step 3 give $H^i(C_Q)=0$ for $i\geq n$. In particular it vanishes for $i>n-1$; the finite-top-cohomology lemma with $m=n-1$ makes $H^{n-1}(C_Q)$ a finitely generated $Q_A$-module. This is a finiteness assertion over the polynomial ring, not over the generally non-Noetherian coefficient ring $A$.

proof.text: Apply single-degree coefficient cone cancellation with base ring $D$, algebra $S=R_D$, the surjection $Q_D\twoheadrightarrow R_D$, the existing $L,\gamma$, and parameter $n-1$. Step 3 verifies its Noetherian base hypothesis, and step 4 verifies its two cone hypotheses. Since $R_D$ is finite type over $D$ and $(R_D)\otimes_D A=R_A$, all its rings and the target are the required ones. Obtain a finite type $D$-algebra $D'$ factoring to $A$, a bounded finite-cohomology $L'$ over $(R_D)\otimes_D D'=R\otimes_B D'$, and $\gamma'$ whose normalized scalar-action cone vanishes for $i\geq n-1$. A finite generating list for $D/B$ followed by a finite generating list for $D'/D$ generates $D'$ over $B$. The result is exactly the induction invariant at $n-1$; its Noetherianity at the next iteration follows again from finite-type permanence.

proof.text: If $a\leq b+1$, perform the preceding improvement $b+1-a$ times, a nonnegative integer; if $a>b+1$, keep the zero initial stage. The final stage has cone cohomology zero for every $i\geq a$. Its $D,L,\gamma$ have precisely the stated algebra factorization and bounded finitely generated cohomology. The map is always the normalized $\mu_K(1\otimes\gamma)$ required by the item, because cancellation returns that same formula. The polynomial ring was only a tool for verifying top-obstruction finiteness; the conclusion concerns the cone in $D(R_D)$ as stipulated.
